description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. 1125, by Order No. 22897, dated July 7, 2026, approved the Utility Discount Program Education Working Group’s Consumer Education Program Plan for Fiscal Year 2027.
text:
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA 
1325 G STREET, NW, SUITE 800 
WASHINGTON, DC 20005 

ORDER ON DELEGATED AUTHORITY 

July 7, 2026 

FORMAL CASE NO. 1125, IN THE MATTER OF THE PROMOTION OF THE UTILITY 
DISCOUNT PROGRAMS, Order No. 22897 

I. 
INTRODUCTION 

1. 
By this Order,1 the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia 
(“Commission”) approves the Utility Discount Program Education Working Group’s (“UDPE 
WG”) Consumer Education Program (“CEP”) Plan for Fiscal Year 2027 (“Proposed FY 2027 
CEP”).2 The Commission approves the CEP and the CEP administrative costs contained in the 
Proposed FY 2027 CEP, the Utility Discount Program (“UDP”) administrative budget, and the 
cost allocation among the District of Columbia Water and Sewer Authority (“DC Water”), the 
Potomac Electric Power Company (“Pepco”), and Washington Gas Light Company (“WGL”) for 
the UDP administrative budget as filed. The Commission directs the District Department of 
Energy and Environment (“DOEE”) to continue its monthly reports and to continue to provide the 
UDPE WG with a proposed UDP administrative budget and CEP budget for the next fiscal year 
by December 31, 2026. 

II. 
BACKGROUND 

2. 
In Order No. 16615, the Commission fundamentally changed the education and 
outreach program for low-income consumers to obtain information about and access to the four 
UDPs in the District of Columbia (“District”).3 Rather than hosting a single annual event—the 
Joint Utility Discount Day—to enroll eligible customers, the Commission approved the creation 
of a year-long CEP to continuously educate consumers about the utility discount programs through 
various media channels. Because the CEP operates on the District fiscal year calendar (October 1

through September 30), Order No. 16615 also required that the UDPE WG submit its proposed 
CEP and budget for the next fiscal year by June 30 for Commission review and approval before 
the beginning of the new fiscal year. On June 30, 2026, the UDPE WG filed its unanimous 
Proposed FY 2027 CEP. The Proposed CEP Plan aims to enhance outreach and increase program 
enrollment. 

III. 
DISCUSSION 

A. 
Proposed FY 2027 CEP and UDP Administrative Budget 

3. 
For FY 2027, the UDPE WG seeks to increase opportunities to facilitate program 
enrollment. The UDPE WG continues to emphasize social media, since social media 
advertisements can be tailored to appeal to all District residents but be specifically targeted to 
connect with residents of targeted zip codes and Wards. The UDPE WG contends that social 
media can help leverage the leading promotional tool for the UDP – word of mouth. The UDPE 
WG’s social media vendor also produces detailed quarterly reports showing measurable results 
and metrics.4 

4. 
The UDPE WG proposes some changes to the $100,000 CEP budget allocations. 
The proposed FY 2027 CEP includes: $10,000 for radio advertisements; $20,000 for Washington 
Metropolitan Area Transit Authority (“WMATA”) advertisements; $50,000 for Social Driver, the 
administrator for the CEP social media presence; and $5,000 each for print newspapers El Tiempo 
Latino, Capital Community Newspapers, the Blade, and the Beacon. The UDPE WG indicates that 
UDP advertisements will run on five of Urban One’s stations. The UDPE WG proposes to increase 
the radio budget to be able to purchase advertisements for the new radio show hosted by Russ Parr, 
a popular radio announcer. WMATA advertisements will be placed on local buses, particularly in 
Wards 5, 7, and 8. Banner advertisements at specific Metrorail stations will be added.5 The UDPE 
WG represents that Social Driver will assist with advertisements on Facebook, Twitter (X), and 
Instagram to boost program awareness, drive website traffic, and encourage audience participation 
and engagement.6 The UDPE WG selected El Tiempo to run Spanish UDP advertisements. 
Additional print advertisements will be placed in Capital Community News, a returning vendor as 
well as the Washington Blade and the Beacon, which will be added in FY 2027.7 The UDPE WG 
is continuing to search for a vendor for the Amharic-speaking community.8 Free advertisements 
will continue to run on the District Government’s community cable channels.9

5. 
The UDPE WG also summarizes each member’s independent outreach activities 
planned for FY 2027. Verizon DC’s supplemental outreach activities include education and flyer 
distribution at District community events and the provision of Lifeline information on the Verizon 
DC website and print media. Verizon DC develops and posts consumer advisories in English and 
Spanish at its authorized payment locations.10 

6. 
WGL indicates that its supplemental outreach includes website placement of 
Residential Essential Service (“RES”) and general UDP information, with contact information for 
DOEE, targeted email campaigns, and inclusion of bill inserts in billing materials. WGL also 
coordinates outreach activities with its Consumer Advisory Panel, which distributes UDP 
information to various District organizations, including Advisory Neighborhood Commissions 
(“ANCs”). WGL participates in community events promoting UDP. WGL also notes that as of 
May 2024, RES customers receive a 50% discount on the monthly customer charge during the 
non-heating season (May through October).11 

7. 
Pepco represents that the promotion of its Residential Aid Discount (“RAD”) 
Program and energy assistance awareness is an integral facet of its community outreach. Through 
education and outreach efforts, Pepco makes presentations and distributes literature to various 
community groups regarding payment plans and energy assistance programs, including RAD and 
the related Arrearage Management Program. Pepco intends to promote energy assistance at local 
libraries. Pepco represents that it designs informational marketing materials, media advisories, 
and press releases about energy assistance, including RAD, to distribute and present in the 
community. Pepco indicates that it uses social media to present up-to-date information about 
energy assistance availability. Additionally, information about energy assistance programs is 
incorporated into Pepco’s electronic newsletters and bill inserts and distributed through Pepco’s 
website and business offices. Pepco also engages in targeted email campaigns. Pepco is also 
targeting customers that are more recently eligible due to the change in income requirements by 
attending mixed income level events such as Glover Park Day and Senior Fest. Pepco asserts that 
it meets with members of the Council of the District of Columbia, organizations such as the Urban 
League, civic and citizens’ associations, and ANCs to encourage participation in the UDP.12 

8. 
DC Water promotes the UDP through bill inserts and messages, paid advertising, 
social media campaigns, earned media, and distribution of the DC Water Cares informational flyer. 
This information is on the DC Water website. DC Water participates in in-person events. 
Additionally, DC Water engages with organizations such as the Greater Washington Urban League 
and OPC. DC Water creates targeted campaigns by using bill inserts, direct telephone calls, and 
mailers. DC Water is seeking new community partners and new ways to engage with its 
customers.13

9. 
The Office of the People’s Counsel for the District of Columbia (“OPC”) represents 
that it will continue to inform District utility customers about the UDP. OPC indicates that in FY 
2026 it participated in over 140 outreach events, where OPC encounters District residents of 
varying backgrounds, including seniors, people with disabilities, and limited or non-English 
language-speaking (“LEP/NEP”) customers. As of May 22, 2026, OPC staff opened nearly 3,300 
consumer cases, including nearly 2,200 requests for financial assistance with utility bills, 1,009 
complaints regarding pending disconnections, and 792 cases of utility disconnection. OPC staff 
assist consumers with completing UDP applications, finding additional resources, and entering 
into payment plans. OPC provides UDP information on OPC’s website, www.opc-dc.gov, and 
disseminates information at outreach events. OPC will continue to educate consumers on financial 
assistance programs, conservation techniques, and the importance of budgeting bills. OPC will 
continue these efforts through its comprehensive customer education and outreach program.14 

10. 
Continuing to educate consumers about utility assistance will be an integral part of 
the Commission’s outreach through its Office of Consumer Services (“OCS”). Going forward, 
the Commission will continue to partner with other DC agencies and local organizations to 
promote the UDP. OCS will also distribute information flyers in multiple languages. OCS will 
also analyze pertinent metrics.15 

11. 
In addition to implementing the CEP, DOEE represents that it will promote the 
UDP on its website. DOEE will also partner with the Mayor’s Office on Latino Affairs, the 
Mayor’s Office on African Affairs, and the Mayor’s Office on Asians and Pacific Islanders to 
increase outreach to members of those communities.16 

12. 
Regarding the administration of the CEP, the UDPE WG maintains that it will 
continue to assume responsibility for CEP oversight. The UDPE WG represents that it will 
develop and implement the CEP each year. The UDPE WG asserts that it will prepare the 
educational materials to be distributed as part of the CEP and develop media and other outreach 
strategies. The UDPE WG also participates in the development of UDP marketing materials and 
mailings by DOEE.17 

13. 
The UDPE WG represents that DOEE will remain the financial administrator for 
the CEP. Each of the entities that support the CEP will pay $25,000, a quarter of the CEP budget, 
for the CEP. DOEE will file quarterly invoices with the Commission for reimbursement. For the 
first three quarters of the year, DOEE will file invoices within 30 days of the end of the quarter, 
while for the last quarter, DOEE will file its invoices within 60 days of the end of the fiscal year. 
Upon Commission approval of the invoices, WGL, Pepco, DC Water, and the District of Columbia

Universal Service Trust Fund (“DC USTF”) will make appropriate payments to DOEE via the

14. 
DOEE and the UDPE WG assert that they understand that UDP expenditures must 
be documented so that the DC USTF and other participating utilities have an accounting of funding 
spent on behalf of their respective programs. DOEE commits to providing the UDPE WG with a 
quarterly report of funds spent, including copies of invoices and other documentation. In its annual 
reports filed with the Commission, the UDPE WG will provide an accounting of all UDP 
expenditures.19 

15. 
The Proposed FY 2027 CEP also includes the FY 2027 proposed UDP budget, 
divided into two portions: eligibility administration; and outreach and engagement. Eligibility 
administration involves the provision, receipt, and processing of UDP applications at two centers 
and online. Outreach and engagement services refer to procurement for CEP advertising and 
oversight of the CEP contracts. For FY 2027, DOEE will assign three additional staff to the 
Service Centers to handle the large volume of applications. DOEE indicates that the combined 
budget for both services totals $861,600 in FY 2027. DOEE represents that the proposed UDP 
administrative budget is approximately 2.49% more than the FY 2026 UDP administrative budget. 
The Proposed FY 2027 CEP increases the Personnel line item by 3.9% but makes no other changes 
to administrative expenses. The UDPE WG proposes to retain the 60:25:15 cost allocation split 
for Pepco, WGL, and DC Water for personnel expenses.20 

16. 
For personnel, DOEE proposes that the UDP administrative expenses include 6.0 
FTEs. 5.5 FTEs are funded by Pepco, DC Water, and WGL for UDP administrative expenses, and 
0.5 FTE is funded by the DC USTF, DC Water, Pepco, and WGL for CEP program promotion. 
The UDP administrative expenses fund 20% of salaries for staff processing applications and 10% 
of the salaries of supervisory personnel. Additionally, 10% of one information technology 
specialist’s time is included. DOEE also assigns 50% of the time of one outreach manager, who 
supervises the CEP advertising contracts. The total personnel cost is $640,000: $560,000 for UDP 
program administration and $80,000 for outreach support.21 

17. 
The UDP administrative expenses also include postage, printing, contractual 
services, supplies, and some maintenance cost for the Energy Affordability database and the online 
application portal. The postage line item at $4,500 includes posting and licensing costs for the 
business reply mail permit. The $10,000 printing cost includes development, reproduction, and 
translation of the UDP flyer and the printing costs for the annual renewal letter and UDP 
applications. The $45,000 contractor services line item includes the vendor mailing the renewal 
applications as well as temporary staff to review the returned applications. A $2,100 line item is

18. 
The UDPE WG indicates that the effectiveness of the CEP will be evaluated 
primarily through UDP participation numbers. During the pandemic, the UDPE WG discovered 
that it needs to find new data collection methods to evaluate the effectiveness of the CEP for FY 
2027. The UDPE WG seeks to add advertising referrals and related metrics as another way to 
measure the effectiveness of the CEP.23 

IV. 
DECISION 

19. 
The Commission notes that in 2021, the eligibility threshold for customer 
participation in RES and RAD increased to 80% of the area median income to incentivize greater 
participation.24 The Commission is highly appreciative of the substantial efforts made by the 
UDPE WG to enhance awareness and accessibility of the four UDPs for current and potential 
participants. The UDPE WG has diligently crafted a diverse and cost-effective outreach strategy 
to maximize program visibility and engagement, particularly targeting underserved communities, 
including LEP/NEP households, and newly eligible customers. Discussion of the Proposed FY 
2027 CEP follows. 

A. 
Proposed FY 2027 CEP 

20. 
The Proposed FY 2027 CEP builds on the successes of previous years by continuing 
its focus on innovative social media campaigns, ensuring more immediate and measurable 
feedback on outreach effectiveness. The UDPE WG asserts that the social media advertisements 
allow for targeted tracking of the effectiveness of their outreach efforts, enabling a more immediate 
and precise evaluation of their impact, and proposes to increase its funding social media while 
eliminating paid television advertising. For FY 2027, the UDPE WG also proposes to continue its 
advertising in print, on radio, and on WMATA, providing a variety of advertising media, adding 
more radio advertisements, new print vendors, and new WMATA banner advertisements. The 
UDPE WG seeks to continue UDP advertisements in Spanish in El Tiempo and is also actively 
looking for a media partner in the Amharic-speaking community. 

21. 
Given the meticulous planning and collaborative efforts demonstrated by the UDPE 
WG, the Commission is confident in the positive impact of the proposed CEP and its budget. 
Therefore, the Commission approves the FY 2027 CEP and FY 2027 CEP budget. Focusing on 
social media permits the UDPE WG to have more immediate and direct feedback regarding the 
effectiveness of its advertisements, instead of waiting for results from the customer survey. The 
Commission approves the continuation of advertising in El Tiempo, the additional of two new 
print vendors, and the search for an Amharic media partner. Increasing advertisements for radio

and WMATA diversify the advertising media. The Commission also approves the administrative

22. 
The UDPE WG proposes a UDP administrative budget of $681,600. No member 
of the UDPE WG objects to the UDP administrative budget. Because this budget increases the 
UDP expenses only slightly, the Commission approves the FY 2027 UDP administrative budget. 
The Commission also approves the proposed division of administrative costs (i.e., cost allocation) 
for the UDP included in the Proposed FY 2027 CEP, ensuring that the financial responsibilities 
are fairly distributed among the participating utilities, since no member of the UDPE WG has 
objected. 

B. 
Reporting 

23. 
Over the years, the Commission has added several reporting requirements to 
improve its oversight of the CEP and the UDP administrative budget.25 Because these reports 
provide the UDPE WG and the Commission with valuable information, the Commission continues 
to require the filing of these reports. 

THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED THAT: 

24. 
The Consumer Education Program Plan and Consumer Education Plan budget for 
Fiscal Year 2027 contained in the Consumer Education Program for Fiscal Year 2027 are 
APPROVED as filed; 

25. 
The Utility Discount Program administrative budget for Fiscal Year 2027 contained 
in the Consumer Education Program for Fiscal Year 2027 is APPROVED as filed; and 

26. 
The District Department of Energy and Environment shall continue to file monthly 
reports required by the Commission in this docket.
